title: A method based on light scattering to estimate the concentration of virus particles without the need for virus particle standards☆
author: Makra, Terejánszky, et al.

steps.title: Prepare virus sample
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the poliovirus stock through a 100 kDa Sartorius Vivaspin 500 centrifugal concentrator three times using an Eppendorf 5430R centrifuge at 13,000 × g, then dilute the retentate with PBS + 0.05 % Tween‑20 (pH 7.4) to one‑third of the original stock concentration.

steps.title: Select latex nanoparticle standards
steps.instruction: Choose commercially available spherical latex nanoparticles with diameters ≤ 73 nm (e.g., 25 nm, 45 nm, 73 nm) because they satisfy the Rayleigh condition (particle diameter < 1/10 × 633 nm laser wavelength). Avoid larger particles such as 330 nm which are not Rayleigh scatterers.

steps.title: Prepare standard dilutions
steps.instruction: Make a series of latex nanoparticle solutions covering concentrations that give scattered‑light intensities between the instrument detection limit (~200 kcps) and the onset of multiple scattering (where intensity no longer increases linearly).

steps.title: Measure scattered intensities
steps.instruction: Using a Zetasizer Nano ZS (red laser, 633 nm) in static‑light‑scattering mode, record the scattered‑light intensity (in kcps) for each standard dilution and for the virus sample, keeping all measurements within the verified linear range.

substeps.instruction: Check linearity of intensity versus concentration for each standard; discard data outside the linear region.
Ensure virus sample intensity also lies within the linear range.

steps.title: Determine slope of standard curve
steps.instruction: Plot intensity (kcps) versus known standard concentration for each nanoparticle size, fit the linear portion, and calculate the slope S = ΔI_standard / Δc_standard (kcps · mL · particle⁻¹).

steps.title: Obtain particle parameters
steps.instruction: Gather the following values: d_standard (latex diameter, e.g., 25, 45, or 73 nm), d_virus (virus diameter from literature or EM/NTA/RPS), n_standard (refractive index of latex, supplied by manufacturer), n_solution (refractive index of PBS + 0.05 % Tween‑20, measured with a refractometer or taken from tables), and n_virus (estimated refractive index, use 1.58 ± 0.04 as justified for poliovirus).

steps.title: Calculate virus concentration
steps.instruction: Insert the measured I_virus, the slope S, the diameter ratio (d_standard/d_virus)^6, and the refractive‑index term [(n_standard/n_solution)^2 − 1 / (n_standard/n_solution)^2 + 2 × (n_virus/n_solution)^2 + 2 (n_virus/n_solution)^2 − 1]^2 into Equation 2: c_virus = I_virus × S × (d_standard/d_virus)^6 × [ … ]^2, yielding the virus concentration in particles · mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Validate and average results
steps.instruction: Repeat the calculation using each of the three Rayleigh‑compliant latex sizes (25, 45, 73 nm) as the standard; compare the resulting c_virus values and report the mean and standard deviation. Confirm that the calculated concentration agrees with independent measurements (e.g., RPS value of (6.5 ± 1.8) × 10¹² mL⁻¹).

description:
The method is based on the Rayleigh approximation which states that if the diameter of the light scatterer is smaller than ca. 1/10th of the wavelength of the light source then the scattered light intensity depends on the scatterer concentration, diameter, and its refractive index relative to the solution refractive index. Thus by having two types of nanoparticles (e.g., latex and virus particles) which have different, but known diameters and refractive indices, one can determine the concentration of one of them (e.g., virus) if the concentration of the other (e.g., latex) is known by measuring the respective scattered light intensities. By this the concentration of the virus is referenced against the concentration of a conveniently chosen nanoparticle standard without the need for virus particle concentration standards that are very difficult to obtain. The expression for the calculation of virus particle concentration was adapted from Vysotskii et al., [1]:(1)cvirus=cstandardIvirusIstandard(dstandarddvirus)6[(nstandard/nsolution)2−1(nstandard/nsolution)2+2×(nvirus/nsolution)2+2(nvirus/nsolution)2−1]2where cvirus is the virus concentration, dvirus and dstandard are the virus and the standard nanoparticle diameter, Ivirus and Istandard are the scattered light intensities stemming from the virus and the nanoparticle standards, nsolution,
nstandard and nvirus are the refractive indices of the solution, the standard particles and the virus, respectively. The expression is valid for virus and standard nanoparticles that are Rayleigh scatterers. We have brought Eq.
